- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast marginally, especially if recent prices are falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after strong upward sentiment spikes; apply a 5–10% downward correction to forecast peak values.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope or add a downward bias in second half of forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, apply downward pressure; if <10% below, consider upward adjustment.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to lag by 1–3 days in reaction to sentiment shifts; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.33” values, model underperforms; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for low sentiment bias.
